questions.solution:

cos2 35° + cos 55°. sin 35° + (tan34°)/(cot56°) = __ __ .

Concept used:

1. sin θ = cos (90° - θ)

2. tan θ = cot (90° - θ)

3. sin² θ + cos² θ = 1

Calculation: 

cos2 35° + cos 55°. sin 35° + (tan34°)/(cot56°)

⇒ cos2 35° + cos (90 - 35)°. sin 35° + (tan34°)/(cot(90 - 34)°)

⇒ cos2 35° + sin 35°. sin 35° + (tan34°)/(tan34°)

⇒ cos2 35° + sin² 35° + 1

⇒ 1 + 1 = 2

∴ The simplified value is 2.

questions.question: A certain sum of money becomes triple of itself in 26 years at simple interest. In how many years it will becomes five times of itself?
questions.solution:
Given:

A certain sum of money becomes triple of itself in 26 years at simple interest. 

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the interest rate be R%.

​According to the question,

(P × R × 26)/100 = 3P - P

⇒ (P × R × 26)/100 = 2P

⇒ R = 100/13

Let's suppose, it will take T years for the principal amount to be five times of itself.

​According to the question,

(P × 100/13 × T)/100 = (5P - P)

⇒ T = 13 × 4

⇒ T = 52

∴ it will take 52 years for the principal amount to be five times of itself.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 5(1)/(3)km/h. It is found that the boat takes thrice as much time to row up than it does to row down the same distance in the river stream. Find the speed of the river stream.
questions.solution:
Given:

The speed of a boat in still water is 5(1)/(3) km/h.

It is found that the boat takes thrice as much time to row up than it does to row down the same distance in the river stream. 

Concept used:

1. While rowing upstream, the upstream speed is the difference between the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the flow.

2. While rowing downstream, the downstream speed is the addition of the speed of the boat in still water and the speed of the flow.

3. Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

Let the distance and the speed of the stream be D and R respectively.

​According to the question,

frac {D}{(16)/(3) - R} = frac {3D}{(16)/(3) + R}

⇒ frac {1}{(16)/(3) - R} = frac {3}{(16)/(3) + R}

⇒ frac {16}{3} + R = 16 - 3R

⇒ 4R = 16 - frac {16}{3}

⇒ R = 8/3

Now, the speed of the stream in m/s = 8/3 × 5/18 = frac {20}{27} m/s​

**∴ The speed of the river stream is frac {20}{27} m/sec.**

questions.question: The largest five-digit number which when divided by 7, 9 and 11, leaves the same remainder as 3 in each case, is :
questions.solution:
Given:

The required largest five-digit number when divided by 7, 9, and 11, leaves the same remainder as 3.

Concept used:

LCM is the smallest common multiple of two or more numbers.

Calculation:

LCM(7, 9, 11) = 693

Largest five-digit number = 99999

Quotient when 99999 is divided by 693 = 144

The largest five-digit number that is divisible by 7, 9, and 11 = 144 × 693 = 99792

Now, the required number = 99792 + 3 = 99795

∴ The required number is 99795.

questions.question: ΔABC and ΔDEF are congruent respectively. If AB = 6 = DE, BC = 8 = EF and m ∠B = 30°, then m ∠D + m ∠C = __ __ .
questions.solution:
Given:

ΔABC and ΔDEF are congruent respectively. 

AB = 6 = DE, BC = 8 = EF and m ∠B = 30°

Concept used:

1. SAS Congruency: If two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to two sides and included angle of another triangle, then the triangles are congruent. E.g.: if ∠A = ∠X and AB/XY = AC/XZ then ΔABC ≅ ΔXYZ.

From the congruency, 

AB/XY = BC/YZ = AC/XZ

and ∠B = ∠Y and ∠C = ∠Z

2. The three interior angles of a triangle will always have a sum of 180°.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b260f67f751e5db4e9f5c34668912ac09fda2ab241783a7ac7d7ef81e61aff55.png] 

​According to the concept,

Since ΔABC and ΔDEF are congruent and AB = 6 = DE, BC = 8 = EF and m ∠B = 30°, m ∠B = m ∠E = 30°.

Also, m ∠C = m ∠F ....(1)

Hence, m ∠A = m ∠D ....(2)

​According to the concept,

m ∠C + m ∠A = (180 - 30)° ....(3)

m ∠E + m ∠F = (180 - 30)° ....(4)

From 1, 2, 3 and 4,

m ∠D + m ∠C = (180 - 30)° 

⇒ m ∠D + m ∠C = 150° 

**∴ The value of m ∠D + m ∠C is 150°.**

questions.question: A dishonest dealer sells a product at 11% loss on cost price, but uses 22% less weight. What is his percentage profit or loss?
questions.solution:
Given:

A dishonest dealer sells a product at an 11% loss on cost price but uses 22% less weight.

Concept used:

1. Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 - Loss%)

2. Profit% = {(Selling Price - Cost Price) over Cost Price} times 100\%

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the product be Rs. 1/gm.

Cost price of 1000gm = Rs. 1000

Selling price of 1000gm = 1000 × (1 - 11%) = Rs. 890

Since he's using 22% less weight, the selling price of the net quantity sold

⇒ 1000 × (1 - 22%) × 1 = Rs. 780

Now, profit% = frac {890 - 780}{780} times 100\% ≈ 14.10%

**∴ His percentage gain is 14.10%.**

Weighted average, W = frac {sum^nᵢ ₌ ₁ X_iW_i}{sum^nᵢ ₌ ₁ W_i}

W = weighted average

n = number of terms to be averaged

His combined loss percentage

⇒ frac {10 times 2 - 20 times 3}{2 + 3}(Loss is taken in a negative manner in contrast to the profit)

⇒ -8% (Negative sign indicates loss)

**∴ The combined loss percentage is 8%.**

questions.question: A contractor decided to complete a work in 80 days and employed 60 men at the beginning and 20 men additionally after 20 days and got the work completed as per schedule. If he had not employed the additional men, how many extra days would he have needed to complete the work (round off to the nearest integer)?
questions.solution:
Given:

A contractor decided to complete a work in 80 days and employed 60 men at the beginning and 20 men additionally after 20 days and got the work completed as per schedule.

Concept used:

Total work = Efficiency of each worker × Number of days to finish × Number of total workers

Calculation:

​According to the question,

The contractor employed 60 men at the beginning and 20 men additionally after 20 days. So 80 men are employed for 60 days.

Total work = 20 × 60 + 60 × 80 = 6000 units

So if he had not employed the additional men, the time is taken to complete the work by 60 men

⇒6000 units/ 60

⇒ 100 days

Now, extra days = 100 - 80 = 20 days

**∴ If he had not employed the additional men, 20 extra days he would have needed to complete the work.**

He allows his customer 20% discount on the marked price.

Concept used:

Final percentage change after two successive increments of A% and B% = (A + B + {AB over 100})\%

His profit or loss percentage

⇒ {(20 + (-20) + frac {20 times -20}{100})}\% (Here, the 20% discount is taken as a negative increment in contrast to the 20% mark up)

⇒ -4% (Negative value indicates loss)

∴ He makes a 4% loss.
